text:
jia: noticed weirdness in today's cost card — large cache savings showing up as model-level savings, no route breakdown. spotted while reviewing canary metrics. attaching short query and stacktrace.

sam: on it. can you paste the exact query and the console trace? thinking either the telemetry join lost route_id or the card render collapsed dimensions.

jia: query we used for the sanity check:
```
SELECT coalesce(route_id, 'unknown') AS route_id,
       model_sku,
       SUM(tokens) AS tokens,
       SUM(cache_saved_tokens) AS cache_saved
FROM token_events
WHERE ts BETWEEN now() - interval '1 day' AND now()
GROUP BY route_id, model_sku
ORDER BY cache_saved DESC
LIMIT 50;
```
raw rows: route_id="signup-flow" model_sku="rwd-4g" cache_saved=412300
console card: single row model_sku="rwd-4g" cache_saved=412300, no route listed.

mike: router attaches billing metadata in billing_context header. our normalizer flattens into a scalar billing_key. if billing_key picks model_sku first we lose the route dimension. last change to the normalizer simplified keys to reduce cardinality.

alexa: for UI, this looks like a data bug but could also be UX improvement opportunity. suggestion: show two columns on the cost-card: Observed Savings (raw sum of cache_saved_tokens) and Attributed Savings (our best-effort allocation across route/model). make the attribution behavior explicit in tooltip.

ops-bot: [deploybot] Canary deploy started for platform/ingest @ 2024-10-04T12:34:10Z

sam: mike, can you point to the code in event-normalizer where route might be dropped? i think the function that composes billing_key is here:
```
// pseudo
if (billing_context.model_sku) billing_key = billing_context.model_sku
else billing_key = billing_context.route_id
```
should prefer route when present.

mike: exact snippet i recall is
```
billing_key = billing_context.get('billing_key') || billing_context.get('model_sku')
```
we should change to prefer route: `billing_key = billing_context.get('route_id') || billing_context.get('model_sku')`
also we should emit explicit columns: route_id and model_sku into token_ledger so downstream aggregations can GROUP BY both.

alexa: product question: if we flip behavior, historical tiles in console will re-attribute and could confuse users. propose feature flag `console.per_route_attribution` default false. rollout plan: enable in staging, run for 24h, run backfill for last 7 days into a separate column `attributed_route` so the UI can toggle between old and new attribution.

jia: ok I'll open PR with changes to normalizer + token_ledger schema change + feature flag. PR will include migration plan notes. will add a note to the cost-card tooltip: "Attribution may change during rollout; toggle per-route view in settings."

sam: tests: add unit tests where two events same model_sku, different route_id should split cache_saved proportionally per route when aggregator groups by route. also add e2e that flips feature flag and asserts UI shows additional column and drilldown links.

mike: watchlist: cardinality explosion. cap per-card route breakdown to top-5 routes by savings and bucket rest as "other". aggregator should compute top-N routes server-side to avoid heavy UI requests.

alexa: UI will render top-5 + other row and a small latency badge: "enabling per-route attribution may add ~10-20ms to cost queries." include a tooltip explaining top-N bucketing and the toggle.

jia: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/2141 (draft). will push tests and migration soon.

sam: once PR is up, ping me. I'll run the unit/integration harness and sanity-check staging before canary.

mike: I'll also sketch an async backfill that writes attributed_route into token_ledger for last 7 days; backfill job will run with low priority and emit progress metrics so we can monitor.

alexa: will mock screenshots and attach to PR for product review. also adding changelog entry to Console -> Cost Cards.

jia: plan: land PR in dev branch, enable feature flag in staging for 24h canary, run backfill, then enable in prod for 10% rollout, observe anomalies for 48h before full rollout. filing TODOs in PR.

sam: good plan. one more ask: add a small anomaly alert that triggers if attributed savings shift >20% for any tenant in a 1h window post-rollout.

mike: ack, will add a metric to the migration job and aggregator to emit percent-delta per-tenant.

jia: thanks all. will update thread with PR links and staging results. :rocket:
